items.title: Trump’s New Favorite Neighbor: Mexico
items.summary: President Trump built his political brand in part on bashing Mexico. Now his second presidency depends on deepening partnerships with the country.

items.title: U.N. Live Updates: Iran’s President Accuses U.S. and Israel of Lawless Attacks
items.summary: Masoud Pezeshkian was the first leader whose country is at war with the United States to address the General Assembly in New York. He decried attacks on civilian targets and said Iran would not accept limits on its nuclear program.

items.title: How China’s Leader Plans to Win the Future With A.I.
items.summary: A decade ago, Xi Jinping asked if China could master A.I. His push is remaking the economy, challenging the United States and keeping society under control.

items.title: Why Germany’s Leader Merz Is Struggling to Sway Voters
items.summary: As the far right surges, Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s unpopular economic policies and gruff manner have failed to sway voters turned by rivals’ promises of easy fixes.

items.title: The Winner of This Rivalry Gets Ice Cream. But So Does the Loser.
items.summary: The competition between two popular ice cream shops in Ramallah inspires fierce loyalties, and a running joke, for lovers of cones piled high with flavors.

items.title: U.S. Rebukes Australia Over Proposed Limits on Social Media Algorithms
items.summary: The U.S. Embassy said a draft law allowing users to opt out of systems that choose what they can see in their feeds could amount to censorship.

items.title: Youth Frustration and Migration Shadow Morocco’s Election
items.summary: Unemployment and poor public services fueled the border crisis at Ceuta and Gen Z protests, but frustrated young people may stay away from the polls.

items.title: At the U.N., Japan’s Leader Says It’s Time to End ‘Enemy State’ Label
items.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the United Nations should scrub the World War II-era designation from its Charter. China and Russia have used the term recently to attack Japan.

items.title: Sri Lanka Convicts 15 in Easter 2019 Bomb Attacks
items.summary: A court found 15 men guilty of coordinating a series of suicide bombings in hotels and churches, which killed more than 300 people.

items.title: Ethiopian Rebel Groups Join Forces Against the Government
items.summary: Half a dozen groups, accusing the prime minister of being dictatorial, announced the formation of a coalition in a country already scarred by war.

items.title: Trump’s Diesel Dilemma
items.summary: Calls to ban U.S. exports of the fuel are dividing Republicans. The energy crisis is also dominating discussions at the United Nations.

items.title: White House Defends Trump’s Ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico in Court Filing
items.summary: President Trump determined that CNN, MS NOW and Politico were in “violation of the standards of professionalism and decorum” expected at the White House.

items.title: Qantas’s New York-to-Sydney ‘Project Sunrise’ Flights to Take Off in 2028
items.summary: Qantas Airways said the 18-hour flights, part of its Project Sunrise program, would come months after its 22-hour direct flights from Sydney to London begin.

items.title: Billy Bush Joins Fox News a Decade After ‘Access Hollywood’ Tape Scandal
items.summary: He lost his job as a “Today” show anchor in 2016 after footage surfaced of Donald J. Trump joking with him about sexual assault. He will be a Fox contributor.

items.title: Trump Says He Supports Banning Diesel Exports to Bring Down Prices
items.summary: Diesel prices have been setting records because of the war in Iran, but the oil industry say banning U.S. exports would not make the fuel cheaper.

items.title: Rosie O’Donnell Says ABC Delayed a Skit as It Readied Trump Suit
items.summary: The network asked the comedian to hold off on the sketch, which mocked the president, when she filled in as host of “Jimmy Kimmel Live!”

items.title: How Paramount Won Warner Bros.
items.summary: After months of legal and political wrangling, the media mogul David Ellison arrived at a deal with the coalition of states seeking to block his $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.

items.title: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Topples Mariah Carey’s Chart Record
items.summary: The country ballad holds the No. 1 spot on the Billboard chart for a 23rd nonconsecutive week, besting the record set by “All I Want for Christmas Is You.”

items.title: Trump Officials Eject 750,000 From Obamacare Markets, Claiming Fraud
items.summary: Vice President JD Vance said the measure would save the government $2.2 billion.

items.title: Trump Is Back on TV, Briefly, as Many Networks Carry His U.N. Speech Live
items.summary: A suspension of pool coverage remains in effect. But the in-house United Nations broadcaster provided a feed of the president’s remarks.

items.title: I Gave My Life Over to Meta’s A.I. Agent and Was Blown Away
items.summary: Muse, Meta’s A.I. agent, helped handle my dental insurance, booked dinner reservations and created a podcast for me. It also required my most personal data, and trust.

items.title: An A.I. Image of Trump Kissing a Woman Was Fake. It Spread Anyway.
items.summary: Advances in artificial intelligence and the myriad ways content is shared online have made establishing authenticity even more difficult for users of social media.

items.title: Anthropic Releases a New A.I. Model, Opus 5.5, Amid Safety Debate
items.summary: The company released a cheaper, faster model that it said was the strongest performer on its most rigorous internal safety tests to date.

items.title: What to Know About Recent A.I. Hacks at Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta
items.summary: OpenAI, Google and others recently disclosed breaches by their artificial intelligence models that amplified concerns about the advancing capabilities of the technology.

items.title: An Army of Paid Creators Is Carpeting the Web With Political Content
items.summary: Unlike celebrity influencers with large followings, these creators produce a blizzard of videos for a fraction of the cost of traditional online campaigns and, in the process, shift public conversation.

items.title: The Big Threat Has Been Climate Change. Now Comes A.I.
items.summary: Both are human-caused, both are frightening, and one of them has raced to the forefront of the global conversation.

items.title: How to Split Expenses on a Group Trip Without Fighting
items.summary: From bachelorette trips to family vacations, group travel can cause relationship-ending fallouts. Here’s how to navigate difficult conversations about finances.

items.title: As Computers Take the Driver’s Seat, Experts Worry About Safety
items.summary: Self-driving systems are getting so good that drivers may overestimate the technology and not be prepared to respond when something goes wrong.

items.title: How Potential 2028 Presidential Candidates Are Talking About A.I.
items.summary: Democrats are jockeying to embrace new safeguards, while Republicans have aligned with President Trump’s warnings against slowing down the technology.

items.title: The A.I. Party House Where Networking Has a Dark Side
items.summary: Group tech houses have proliferated across the San Francisco Bay Area in the artificial intelligence boom. One of the most prominent has also racked up an extensive police record.
